subject: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming SLOs / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming SLOs / next steps

Thanks for the time this morning — great conversation. Recap of the performance/streaming items we agreed to validate and the suggested next steps: 

Summary (what you asked for)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 120-200ms for short prompts (50-150 tokens). For critical user flows we'd like 100ms if possible; 200ms is our upper SLO.
- Sustained throughput: ~50 req/s, with burst to 200 req/s for short windows.
- Concurrency: ~250 concurrent active streaming sessions (browser clients).
- Streaming transport: prefer SSE (EventSource) for browser clients; WebSocket acceptable for mobile/native if SSE is blocked.
- Chunk cadence: target ~200-400ms between first and subsequent chunks for interactive feel; typical chunk sizes 10-50 tokens.
- Failure behavior: graceful degrade to full-response (non-streaming) on fallback; measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and per-chunk latency.

What we need from Acme before the deep technical call:
1) Representative payloads and response size distribution (attach a small set of sample prompts and expected completion sizes).
2) Typical session lifecycle (how long sessions stay open, average tokens per session).
3) Any network constraints (corporate proxies, limited keep-alive, TLS termination details).

Next steps (proposed)
- Acme: send example payloads + traffic shape (JSON).
- Redwood: run a profiling pass with a dedicated small test cluster and share a one-page SLO summary (attached).
- Book a technical deep dive with our infra lead (Aditya) and performance engineer (Neha) — we suggested Thu 14 Jul 10:00 PT.

Attachments: SLO_summary.pdf (high-level perf targets and test plan)

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite once we have the sample traffic.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and captures the asks. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- On TTFT: for certain UX-critical flows we were hoping for <=100ms for very short responses (~20-40 tokens). If that's achievable at P95 with a reasonable config we'd prefer that.
- Chunk cadence: 200-300ms sounds right for chat; for some "live caption" flows we can accept 300-500ms.
- Concurrency: the 250 concurrent sessions is accurate for peak usage in our largest region.

I'll attach a small sample of representative prompts + a short traffic histogram. Expect ~70% of requests under 100 tokens, median response ~60 tokens, 95th approx 240 tokens. Attaching example-traffic.json now.

Can you take a first pass on feasibility and call out any quick wins we could suggest (config recommendations, model variants, quantization, caching, Dedicated vs Hosted)? Key asks from Acme: low TTFT (ideally <=100ms P95 for short replies), ~250 concurrent streaming sessions, burst to 200 req/s.

Initial notes for the deep dive request:
- We'll propose a Dedicated pool to give predictable tail latency; recommend a quantized model variant and prefix/KV caching where possible.
- Streaming: support SSE as first-class option; WebSocket fallback. Ensure our chunk buffering and TLS handshake time keep TTFT within target.
- Batching: to hit throughput without harming TTFT we may need aggressive single-request forwarding up to Xms batch window — Aditya, can you estimate a starting batch window we should test?

Attaching the SLO summary we plan to share.

—
Marissa

Thanks for the context — this is feasible with a clear test plan. Quick tech notes / proposal: 

1) Deployment recommendation\- Start with Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) using a quantized model variant that matches the accuracy profile Acme needs. Dedicated gives the most predictable p99 latency.

2) TTFT and per-chunk latency\- Expect base TTFT to be dominated by TLS + model warmup + token-generation first-step. With a tuned quantized variant and pinned capacity we can target ~80-140ms P95 for short prompts (20-60 tokens) in the best-case region. P99 will depend on network and model size.

3) Streaming transport and chunk cadence\- SSE (EventSource) is ideal for browser clients; WebSocket for mobile/native. We'll implement server-side chunk flush to aim for 200-350ms cadence. We recommend starting tests at 250ms cadence target and iterating.

4) Batching and concurrency\- To preserve TTFT we recommend a very small batching window (<=5-10ms) for interactive flows and a slightly larger window for background flows. We'll measure tradeoffs in the perf test. For concurrency 250 sessions we should provision to support sustained 50 req/s with headroom for spikes to 200 req/s; autoscaling and burst capacity will be configured accordingly.

5) Caching / prefix strategies\- If Acme has repeating prefixes (system prompts or instruction templates) we can use prefix/KV caching to reduce per-request token cost and improve tail latency. Please flag any canonical prompts.

6) Next steps\- a) We'll run an internal profile with the sample traffic and share a results doc (link below). b) Schedule the deep-dive Thu 14 Jul 10:00 PT — Marissa, can you send calendar invite to Jason, Sanjay, Neha, and me? c) If Acme can provide a short test account or allow our perf harness to hit a staging endpoint, we'll run a 2-hour load test to validate TTFT P95/P99 and chunk cadence.
